 This Criminal Petition Is Filed U/Sec. 482 Of Cr.P.C.
Seeking To Quash Entire Proceedings In Badami P.S. Crime
No.06/2013 Registered For The Offences P/U/Sec. 467, 471,
474, 201, 419, 420, 465 And 468 R/W Sec.34 Of Ipc In Cc No.
81/2015 Pending On The File Of Senior Civil Judge And Jmfc
Court, Badami In So Far As Present Petitioners/Accused
No.1, 2 And 4 Are Concerned.
 This Petition, Coming On For Admission, This Day, The
Court Made The Following:
 Order

1. The petitioners are before this Court calling in question the proceedings in CC No.81/2015 registered for the offences punishable under Sections 467, 471, 474, 201, 419, 420, 465 and 468 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as 'the IPC', for short).
2.

During the pendency of the petition, the parties to the lis have settled the dispute amongst themselves and therefore, have filed an application seeking compounding of offences under Section 320 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
The application also appends an affidavit confirming the contents of the said application.

The application reads as follows:
"Application under section 320 R/w 482 of Criminal Procedure Code NC:
2023:KHC-D:10863 The petitioners and respondent no 2 respectfully submit as under:
1. That being aggrieved by the filing entire proceedings in C.C. no 81/2015 pending on the file of Senior Civil Judge and JMFC Badamai, petitioners have filed this Criminal Petition.
2.

It is submitted, the complainant/respondent no 2 had filed a suit in OS No 41/2013 before the Court of Senior Civil Judge and JMFC Badami wherein he has sought for relief of declaration to hold that the sale deed stated 22/7/2012 in respect of suit plot Smt Naseemabhanu vs The State Of Karnataka on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126618098/
2 no 5 and 10 and sale deeds dated 28/11/202 in respect of suit plots no 43, 44 and 50 of Schedule -A of the suit property illegal, void and forged documents created by impersonation and sought for restraining relief the of defendants permanent or injunction anybody claiming under them from interfering with the possession and enjoyment of the Plaintiff over the suit schedule property, the said suit came to be decreed vide order dated 01/06/2022.
3.Thereafter, the present petitioner no 1 who was defendant no 1 in OS NO: 41/2013 had preferred an Regular Appeal in RA No: 31/2023 before the court of District and Sessions Judge, Bagalkot against the present Respondent No 2 (Original Plaintiff in OS No: 41/2013) appeal and others, In the said regular the parties to the lis in view of the intervention by the elders of the village, all of them agreed to compromise the case and accordingly submitted a compromise petition U/O 23 Rule NC:
2023:KHC-D:10863 3 of CPC and accordingly settled the case in between them through the intervention of elders.

entities.text: Naseemabhanu vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
4. When things stood thus, the impugned proceedings in the present criminal petition would not be proceeded further because of settlement arrived at by the respective parties in a civil proceedings and the subject matter of the present criminal and the civil proceedings being proceedings one and the same, this Hon'ble Court may kindly permit the parties to the lis to compound the offences as the offences alleged are not the one which are having impact on the society as a whole.
5.

As per the dictum of the case decided by Honble Apex Court in Gian Singh V State of Punjab wherein it is held, when the offence is civil, where wrong is personal, and the matter is resolved between the parties consensually, proceedings can be quashed by the High Court.

entities.text: Gian Singh V State of Punjab
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: And so also, the High Court can quash the criminal proceedings where the conviction is not possible and the parties are ready to settle the case amongst themselves even if the offence did not fall under compoundable offences.
Therefore in view of the said dictum it is humbly prayed to allow the parties to compound the offences and close the pending criminal case which is impugned in the present criminal petition.

6. The continuation of the proceedings will not result in the order of conviction against the present petitioners as such it would be a futile exercise therefore to allow the proceedings it is just and necessary to continue, to quash NC: 2023:KHC-D:10863 the entire proceedings as it is a clear case of abuse of process of law.
Wherefore the petitioners and the respondent no 2 seek leave of this Honble court to permit them to settle the case and compound the offences and this Honble Court may kindly be pleased to:
(a) Allow the present application.
(b) quash entire proceedings in Badami P S Crime No:
Smt Naseemabhanu vs The State Of Karnataka on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126618098/
3 06/2013 registered for the offences punishable u/secs 467, 471, 474, 201, 419, 420,
465 and 468 r/w sec 34 of IPC in CC No 81/2015 pending on the file Senior Civil Judge and JMFC Court, Badami in so far as present petitioners/accused no 1, 2 and 4 are concerned.

entities.text: Naseemabhanu vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
(c) Pass any other order or direction as deem it fit by this Hon'ble court in the facts and circumstances of the instant case."
3. In the light of the application seeking compounding of the offences as also the fact that the entire issue being seemingly civil in nature, projected as a crime, I deem it appropriate to accept the application and permit compounding of the offence and close the proceedings against the petitioners.
4. For the aforesaid reasons, the following NC: 2023:KHC-D:10863 ORDER i.
The petition is disposed.
ii. The FIR in Crime No.6/2013 of Badami Police Station pending on the file of the learned Senior Civil Judge and JMFC Court, Badami in CC No.81/2015 is quashed qua the petitioners.
